citation: Primary data: CFPB HMDA 2025. Derived figures: Yetis, Z. (2026), FinanceRateCalc. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21575105
verification_note: No figure in this file has been independently reproduced. Specification for checking any of them: https://financeratecalc.com/reconciliation.html. If a figure is wrong it is corrected in public with attribution: https://financeratecalc.com/corrections.html

claims.universe: FHA applications (loan_type 2) reaching a credit decision (action_taken 1,2,3), excluding reverse mortgages; denial = action 3; CFPB HMDA 2025

known_divergences.explain: Restricting the universe to home purchase applications drops the national FHA denial rate from 22.1% to roughly 13%. This is the single largest source of divergence between published FHA figures. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions.
known_divergences.fix: Include all loan purposes, or state that the figure is purchase-only.

known_divergences.explain: 21.7% was published here until 26 July 2026, when reverse mortgages (HECM) were removed from the universe following a methodology review. The corrected figure is 22.1%.
Inside Mortgage Finance reported 22.0% for 2025. The 0.1-point gap is consistent with rounding or a slightly different treatment of edge cases; both figures describe the same universe.
known_divergences.fix: No action needed — this is agreement, not divergence.

known_divergences.cause: withdrawn or incomplete files included in the denominator
known_divergences.explain: Including action_taken 4 (withdrawn) and 5 (closed for incompleteness) inflates the denominator and depresses the rate. Neither represents a credit decision.
known_divergences.fix: Restrict the denominator to action_taken 1, 2 and 3.

known_divergences.explain: 17.6% is the share of all denials issued by the 100 largest lenders that cite incomplete application. 1.8% is the share at the median lender. Both are correct: the first describes the typical denied borrower, the second the typical institution.
1.2% was published until the HECM correction of 26 July 2026. The corrected median is 1.8%.
Figures near 8-10% typically cover all mortgage types rather than FHA alone, and are usually volume-weighted.
known_divergences.fix: Filter to loan_type 2 and state the weighting.

reconcile.how: Compare a figure you have seen against the published value for the same quantity. Where they differ, the cause is usually definitional rather than computational, and the common causes are listed per claim under known_divergences.
reconcile.note: A match is not proof either figure is correct. None of these has been independently reproduced.

minimum_disclosure.note: Six items any published mortgage denial rate should carry. A figure lacking them is not necessarily wrong, but it cannot be reconciled against any other figure.

items.effect: restricting to home purchase drops the national FHA rate from 22.1% to roughly 13%
